short_description.id: Champ atau Champy adalah monster danau dalam cerita rakyat Amerika yang dikatakan hidup di Danau Champlain di antara New York dan Vermont, digambarkan sebagai ular laut berkepala kuda.
short_description.en: Champ, or Champy, is a lake monster of American folklore said to live in Lake Champlain between New York and Vermont, described as a sea serpent with a horse's head.

long_description.id: Champ, juga disebut Champy atau Tatoskok, adalah makhluk air yang konon menghuni Danau Champlain, perairan tawar yang dibagi antara New York dan Vermont dan sebagian masuk ke Quebec. Ia digambarkan sebagai ular laut sepanjang sekitar 20 kaki berkepala kuda, dan telah ada lebih dari 300 laporan penampakan. Cerita aslinya dikaitkan dengan legenda Iroquois tentang ular raksasa yang oleh bangsa Mohawk disebut Onyare'kowa.
long_description.en: Champ, also called Champy or Tatoskok, is a water creature said to inhabit Lake Champlain, a body of fresh water shared by New York and Vermont and reaching into Quebec. It is described as a sea serpent about 20 feet long with a horse's head, and more than 300 sightings have been reported. The original story is tied to Iroquois legends of giant snakes that the Mohawk called Onyare'kowa.

long_description.id: Penjelajah Samuel de Champlain sering dikatakan sebagai orang Eropa pertama yang melihat Champ pada 1609, tetapi tidak ada bukti ia mengatakan hal itu, dan ia hanya mencatat ikan-ikan besar; para kriptozoolog menyimpulkan ia menggambarkan ikan gar. Laporan 1819 menyebut Crum melihat monster sepanjang sekitar 187 kaki, dan pada 1883 Sheriff Nathan H. Mooney mengaku melihat ular air. P. T. Barnum menawarkan hadiah pada 1873 dan 1887.
long_description.en: Explorer Samuel de Champlain is often said to have been the first European to see Champ in 1609, but there is no evidence he said so and he only recorded large fish; cryptozoologists conclude he described a gar. An 1819 report has Crum seeing a monster about 187 feet long, and in 1883 Sheriff Nathan H. Mooney claimed to have seen a water serpent. P. T. Barnum offered rewards in 1873 and 1887.

long_description.id: Pada 1977 Sandra Mansi mengambil foto yang tampak memperlihatkan hewan berleher panjang muncul dari danau; keluarga Mansi melaporkan makhluk berkepala kecil dan berpunuk. Teluk tempat foto itu diambil tidak lebih dalam dari 14 kaki, dan Joe Nickell menilai makhluk raksasa tak mungkin berenang apalagi bersembunyi di sana. Penentang menyebut danau terlalu kecil dan tidak ada bukti fisik, dengan penjelasan berupa tipuan, salah kenal benda mati, dan salah identifikasi hewan.
long_description.en: In 1977 Sandra Mansi took a photograph that appears to show a long-necked animal emerging from the lake, and the Mansis reported a creature with a small head and a humped back. The bay where it was taken is no deeper than 14 feet, and Joe Nickell judged that a giant creature could hardly swim, let alone hide, there. Skeptics cite a lake too small and no physical proof, offering explanations of hoax, confusion with inanimate objects, and misidentified animals.

long_description.id: Pada awal 1980-an Vermont dan New York sama-sama mengesahkan undang-undang yang melindungi habitat dan kehidupan Champ. Legendanya dianggap daya tarik wisata di sekitar Burlington, Vermont, dan Plattsburgh, New York, dan desa Port Henry mendirikan model raksasa serta menggelar Champ Day tiap Agustus.
long_description.en: Vermont and New York both enacted laws in the early 1980s to protect Champ's habitat and life. The legend is considered a tourist draw around Burlington, Vermont, and Plattsburgh, New York, and the village of Port Henry has erected a giant model and holds Champ Day each August.

cultural_context.id: Legenda Champ dianggap daya tarik wisata di wilayah Burlington dan Plattsburgh dan telah menjadi atraksi yang menghasilkan pendapatan.
cultural_context.en: The Champ legend is considered a draw for tourism in the Burlington and Plattsburgh areas and has become a revenue-generating attraction.

statement.en: The original story is related to Iroquois legends of giant snakes, which the Mohawk named Onyare'kowa.

claims.quote: French cartographer Samuel de Champlain, the founder of Québec and the lake's namesake, is often claimed to be the first European to have sighted Champ, in 1609.

statement.id: Samuel de Champlain sering diklaim sebagai orang Eropa pertama yang melihat Champ pada 1609.
statement.en: French cartographer Samuel de Champlain, the founder of Québec and the lake's namesake, is often claimed to be the first European to have sighted Champ, in 1609.

claims.quote: In 1977, Sandra Mansi took a photograph while on vacation with her family that appears to show an animal with a long neck emerging from the lake.

statement.id: Pada 1977, Sandra Mansi mengambil foto saat berlibur bersama keluarganya yang tampak memperlihatkan hewan berleher panjang muncul dari danau.
statement.en: In 1977, Sandra Mansi took a photograph while on vacation with her family that appears to show an animal with a long neck emerging from the lake.

claims.quote: In American folklore, Champ or Champy is the name of a lake monster said to live in Lake Champlain, a 125-mile (201 km)-long body of fresh water shared by New York and Vermont, with a portion extending into Quebec, Canada.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Amerika, Champ atau Champy adalah nama monster danau yang dikatakan hidup di Danau Champlain, perairan tawar sepanjang 125 mil (201 km) yang dibagi antara New York dan Vermont, dengan sebagian membentang ke Quebec, Kanada.
statement.en: In American folklore, Champ or Champy is the name of a lake monster said to live in Lake Champlain, a 125-mile (201 km)-long body of fresh water shared by New York and Vermont, with a portion extending into Quebec, Canada.

claims.quote: Over the years, there have been over 300 reported sightings of Champ.

statement.id: Selama bertahun-tahun, telah ada lebih dari 300 laporan penampakan Champ.
statement.en: Over the years, there have been over 300 reported sightings of Champ.

claims.quote: An 1819 report in the Plattsburgh Republican, entitled "Cape Ann Serpent on Lake Champlain", reports a "Capt. Crum" sighting an enormous serpentine monster. Crum estimated the monster to have been about 187 ft (57 m) long and approximately 200 yd (180 m) away from him.

statement.id: Laporan tahun 1819 di Plattsburgh Republican berjudul 'Cape Ann Serpent on Lake Champlain' menyebut 'Crum' melihat monster ular raksasa; Crum memperkirakan panjangnya sekitar 187 kaki (57 m) dan jaraknya sekitar 200 yard (180 m).
statement.en: An 1819 report in the Plattsburgh Republican, entitled 'Cape Ann Serpent on Lake Champlain', reports a 'Capt. Crum' sighting an enormous serpentine monster, which Crum estimated to be about 187 ft (57 m) long and about 200 yd (180 m) away.

claims.quote: In 1883, Sheriff Nathan H. Mooney claimed that he had seen a water serpent about "20 rods" (the equivalent of 110 yd (100 m) in length) from where he was on the shore.

statement.id: Pada 1883, Sheriff Nathan H. Mooney mengaku melihat ular air sekitar '20 rod' (setara 110 yard atau 100 m) dari tempatnya berdiri di tepi danau.
statement.en: In 1883, Sheriff Nathan H. Mooney claimed that he had seen a water serpent about '20 rods' (the equivalent of 110 yd (100 m)) from where he was on the shore.

claims.quote: The legend of Champ captured the interest of P. T. Barnum, and in 1873 and 1887, the famous showman offered rewards for anyone who could bring him the monster.

statement.id: Legenda Champ menarik minat P. T. Barnum, dan pada 1873 serta 1887 sang pemain sirkus terkenal menawarkan hadiah bagi siapa pun yang dapat membawakan monster itu kepadanya.
statement.en: The legend of Champ captured the interest of P. T. Barnum, and in 1873 and 1887 the famous showman offered rewards for anyone who could bring him the monster.

claims.quote: The earliest source for this claim is the summer 1970 issue of the magazine Vermont Life. The magazine quoted Champlain as having documented a "20 ft (6.1 m) serpent thick as a barrel, and a head like a horse." There is no evidence that Champlain ever said this, although he did document large fish

statement.id: Sumber paling awal klaim itu adalah majalah Vermont Life edisi musim panas 1970, yang mengutip Champlain telah mencatat 'ular 20 kaki (6,1 m) setebal tong dengan kepala seperti kuda', tetapi tidak ada bukti bahwa Champlain pernah mengatakannya, meski ia memang mencatat ikan-ikan besar.
statement.en: The earliest source for the claim is the summer 1970 issue of the magazine Vermont Life, which quoted Champlain as having documented a '20 ft (6.1 m) serpent thick as a barrel, and a head like a horse'; there is no evidence that Champlain ever said this, although he did document large fish.

claims.quote: The entire bay of the lake where the photograph reportedly was taken is no deeper than 14 feet (4.3 m). According to Joe Nickell, it is unlikely that a giant creature could swim, let alone hide, in such shallow water.

statement.id: Seluruh teluk danau tempat foto itu konon diambil tidak lebih dalam dari 14 kaki (4,3 m); menurut Joe Nickell, sulit bagi makhluk raksasa untuk berenang, apalagi bersembunyi, di perairan sedangkal itu.
statement.en: The entire bay of the lake where the photograph reportedly was taken is no deeper than 14 feet (4.3 m); according to Joe Nickell, it is unlikely that a giant creature could swim, let alone hide, in such shallow water.

claims.quote: The Champ legend has become a revenue-generating attraction. For example, the village of Port Henry, New York, has erected a giant model of Champ and holds "Champ Day" on the first Saturday of every August.
claims.locator: Cultural importance to New York and Vermont

statement.id: Legenda Champ telah menjadi daya tarik penghasil pendapatan; misalnya desa Port Henry, New York, mendirikan model Champ raksasa dan menggelar 'Champ Day' pada Sabtu pertama setiap Agustus.
statement.en: The Champ legend has become a revenue-generating attraction; for example, the village of Port Henry, New York, has erected a giant model of Champ and holds 'Champ Day' on the first Saturday of every August.

claims.quote: Champ is also known as Champy and Tatoskok; it is a water creature that allegedly lives in Lake Champlain, a 490-square-mile lake located between the U.S. states of New York and Vermont.

statement.id: Champ juga dikenal sebagai Champy dan Tatoskok; ia makhluk air yang konon hidup di Danau Champlain, danau seluas 490 mil persegi di antara negara bagian AS New York dan Vermont.
statement.en: Champ is also known as Champy and Tatoskok; it is a water creature that allegedly lives in Lake Champlain, a 490-square-mile lake between the U.S. states of New York and Vermont.

claims.quote: As of 2015, there have been over 300 alleged sightings of Champ: it is described as an approximately 20-foot-long sea serpent with the head of a horse. Cryptozoologists report that Champ may be of the same lineage as the famous Loch Ness Monster of Scotland.

statement.id: Hingga 2015 ada lebih dari 300 dugaan penampakan Champ; ia digambarkan sebagai ular laut sepanjang sekitar 20 kaki berkepala kuda, dan para kriptozoolog menyebut Champ mungkin segaris keturunan dengan Monster Loch Ness yang terkenal di Skotlandia.
statement.en: As of 2015 there have been over 300 alleged sightings of Champ; it is described as an approximately 20-foot-long sea serpent with the head of a horse, and cryptozoologists report that Champ may be of the same lineage as the famous Loch Ness Monster of Scotland.

claims.quote: Cryptozoologists, examining the journals that de Champlain wrote, concluded that he was describing a fish, the garfish, which is native to the region.

statement.id: Para kriptozoolog yang memeriksa jurnal de Champlain menyimpulkan bahwa ia menggambarkan ikan, yaitu ikan gar yang asli wilayah itu.
statement.en: Cryptozoologists, examining the journals that de Champlain wrote, concluded that he was describing a fish, the garfish, which is native to the region.

claims.quote: The Mansis reported seeing a creature with a small head, long neck, and a humped back approximately eight feet out of the water. The entire amount of time that Champ was above water was reportedly no more than seven minutes.

statement.id: Keluarga Mansi melaporkan melihat makhluk berkepala kecil, berleher panjang, dan berpunuk sekitar delapan kaki di atas air; seluruh waktu Champ berada di atas air dilaporkan tidak lebih dari tujuh menit.
statement.en: The Mansis reported seeing a creature with a small head, long neck, and humped back about eight feet out of the water, and the whole time Champ was above water was reportedly no more than seven minutes.

claims.quote: In 1977, the Mansi photograph surfaced, which appeared to be documented proof of Champ’s existence. In the early 1980s both Vermont and New York passed laws protecting the habitat and life of Champ.

statement.id: Pada 1977 foto Mansi muncul dan tampak sebagai bukti terdokumentasi keberadaan Champ; pada awal 1980-an Vermont dan New York sama-sama mengesahkan undang-undang yang melindungi habitat dan kehidupan Champ.
statement.en: In 1977 the Mansi photograph surfaced, which appeared to be documented proof of Champ's existence; in the early 1980s both Vermont and New York passed laws protecting the habitat and life of Champ.

claims.quote: The theories that attempt to disprove Champ’s existence rely on the facts that the lake is not large enough for a creature of Champ’s size to hide and survive; ... and that there is no physical proof of Champ’s existence.

statement.id: Teori yang membantah keberadaan Champ bertumpu pada fakta bahwa danau tidak cukup besar bagi makhluk seukuran Champ untuk bersembunyi dan bertahan hidup, dan bahwa tidak ada bukti fisik keberadaan Champ.
statement.en: The theories that attempt to disprove Champ's existence rely on the facts that the lake is not large enough for a creature of Champ's size to hide and survive, and that there is no physical proof of Champ's existence.

claims.quote: There are several possible explanations that are posited to explain the nature of the photographs, video, and testimony for Champ. The three major categories of explanations are hoaxes, confusion with inanimate objects, and misidentification of other animals.

statement.id: Ada beberapa penjelasan yang diajukan untuk foto, video, dan kesaksian tentang Champ; tiga kategori utamanya adalah tipuan, salah kenal dengan benda mati, dan salah identifikasi hewan lain.
statement.en: Several explanations are posited for the photographs, video, and testimony for Champ; the three major categories are hoaxes, confusion with inanimate objects, and misidentification of other animals.
